title: Accuracy Sentry: consensus-based validation harness for quant profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a consensus-based automated accuracy validation harness ("Sentry") that evaluates candidate quantization profiles (FP8, INT8) against a curated golden prompt set and multiple orthogonal metrics, and produces deterministic pass/fail gates for canary and rollout automation. Unlike previous single-metric checks, this harness computes a weighted consensus across n metrics, applies variance-aware thresholds, and emits human-readable justification and tooling artifacts for postmortems and rollouts. Goals: 1) Surface regressions introduced by quant/compilation choices early in CI/canary, 2) Provide stable, explainable pass/fail signals for automated rollouts, 3) Reduce manual calibration cycles by >=50% for new model variants.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness runs in CI and Canary pipelines and completes within defined SLA (<= 30m for a 200-prompt golden set). 2) For a curated set of historical quant changes, harness reproduces known pass/fail outcomes with >=95% fidelity. 3) Outputs include a single verdict (PASS/FAIL), a ranked list of offending prompts, per-metric deltas, confidence score, and suggested mitigations file. 4) Integration hooks for Console to show per-route validation status and links to detailed artifacts.
implementation_notes: - Use existing golden corpus 'gp-set-v3' stored in gs://redwood-evals/golden/gp-set-v3. - Metrics to compute: token-level logprob delta, sequence perplexity delta, embedding cosine drift (SBERT), KL divergence of next-token distribution, BLEU/ROUGE for structured outputs, and hallucination detector score. - Consensus scoring: normalize metric deltas, apply per-metric weights (configurable via YAML), compute robust median and variance-aware multiplier. - Pass/fail gating: thresholded consensus score plus rule-based overrides (e.g., if hallucination delta > 4x baseline then automatic fail). - Per-profile calibration: run 3 randomized seeds to estimate nondeterministic variance; require pass across median and 90th percentile of seeds. - Store artifacts in artifacts/<profile>/<run_ts>/ with signed URLs. - Telemetry: quant-validation-metrics.{consensus_score,metric_deltas,run_duration,seed_variance}. - Ensure harness can be invoked in k8s job or as a serverless batch worker. - Keep runtime-local ops idempotent and cache model downloads to reduce repeated setup time.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for metric calculators with synthetic distributions and edge cases. 2) Integration test that runs harness on a trimmed gp-set-v3 (20 prompts) to validate output schema. 3) Regression suite: replay three historical quant regressions stored in /regressions/ and verify verdicts match incident learnings. 4) Canary smoke: integrate with canary-runner to validate a FP8 profile on a small traffic slice and confirm automations receive PASS/FAIL webhooks. 5) Load test: run 200-prompt harness on CI runner to confirm completion time < 30m.

2025-02-18 — Marco Nguyen: spike completed. Found that embedding cosine drift correlates poorly with token-logprob for short prompts; added SBERT-large and a response-normalized cosine to improve signal. Spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QUANT/consensus-spike-2025-02-18.

2025-02-25 — Infra (Liam O'Connor): provisioning a GPU CI runner for canary harness. PR for k8s job spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/314.

2025-02-28 — Marco Nguyen: integrated metric normalization and weights config. Ran end-to-end on fp8-profile-2025-02 and produced expected FAIL for known bad profile. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant/pull/789 — awaiting review.

2025-03-01 — PM Feedback (Rina Gupta): requested explicit UI contract for Console (what fields are required for the per-route view). Added acceptance criterion to include links and suggested mitigations file.
2025-03-01 — QA (Diego Alvarez): flagged nondeterministic failures on seed=7 during regression runs; proposed running 3 seeds and using median plus variance filter (implemented).
notes: Trade-offs considered: heavyweight semantic metrics (SBERT) increase runtime but improve false positive reduction; we tuned to run SBERT only on prompts flagged by faster heuristics to keep average runtime low. Future work: adaptive golden set sampling and automatic threshold tuning using production traffic fingerprints.
